lesson.text: Quick memory: how do you unplug safely? (Hold the plug, not the cable.) Today: the fuse box, someone stuck to electricity, and a fallen power line.
The fuse box is where the electricity comes into a home. Its main switch turns all the power off. An RCD is a safety switch that turns off fast if something is wrong.
Someone stuck to electricity: never touch them, or it goes through you too. Switch off at the fuse box if you can reach it safely, and call {number}.
A fallen power line can still be live, and the ground around it too. Stay at least 10 metres away, keep others away, and call {number}.
Not for a child to do: touching or moving a power line, even with a stick. A cracked plug or loose cable: stop using it until it is mended.
Try it in the world: open the practice house and the park after the storm. Then find your own fuse box with a grown-up.

exercises.explain: It turns all the power in the home off.

exercises.prompt: You should grab someone who is stuck to electricity.
exercises.hint: It would go through you too.

exercises.prompt: A power line lies on the path. You...
choices: stay far away and tell a grown-up
switches off fast if something is wrong
exercises.explain: It switches off fast if electricity goes the wrong way.

exercises.prompt: Pressing an RCD's test button should switch it off.
exercises.explain: True: then switch it back on.

exercises.prompt: Someone is stuck to electricity: put it in order.
items: switch off at the fuse box if it is safe
exercises.explain: Don't touch, switch off if safe, call.

items: staying 10 metres from a fallen line
poking the line with a stick
exercises.explain: Far away and warning others: safe.

exercises.prompt: A plug's case is cracked. You...
choices: stop using it until it is mended

exercises.prompt: The ground near a fallen power line can be live too.
exercises.explain: True: even near it is not safe.

exercises.prompt: Who moves a fallen power line?
choices: a child with a dry stick
exercises.hint: Not for a child to do.
